title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1LC0RA_1LD0RC_1LE1LF_1LA0LC_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1LC0RA_1LD0RC_1LE1LF_1LA0LC_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is a macro machine on lists of numbers: the tape at the left end is A>1 (10)^N sep (10)^w1 sep … (10)^wk sep W, and one sweep takes the fuel N to N−2 and rewrites the start of W by one of a dozen local rules. Lean (kernel) proves such a sweep, with the done blocks w1…wk arbitrary (any number, any values ≥ 2), for the window rules that carry the run; the machine has no halting move inside them. The full list of rules (py/mac14.py) is checked against the machine for 2·107 steps sweep by sweep and at all 33 refills up to 1010 steps, and runs 187,450 sweeps without meeting a case it does not cover. Not proved: the rare fuel-1 sweep and windows with small values, and above all that the run never leaves the rules.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: The cell pieces of a sweep
claims.text: Leaving the left end (start_s, start_z), crossing a done block going right (rb) and coming back (lbA, lbD for values ≥ 4, lb3A … lb2D for 3 and 2), the end at the left (endA_s … endD_0), 14 window rules and the pair rule on the fuel block, each for every value of its counts and every tape around it. Written by bbtools.symtm.prove.

claims.title: One sweep over any list of done blocks
claims.text: sweep_gen: for fuel n+3, any list of done blocks of values ≥ 2 and any window rule that turns back in state A, the machine goes from cfg (n+3) ds W to cfg (n+1) ds W'. sweep_gen2 (fuel 2 → 0) and sweep_gen0 (fuel 0: refilled to 2) likewise. Proved by induction over the list (rpass, lpass).

claims.title: The window rules
claims.text: With fuel ≥ 3 and any done blocks: the pair rule x s y → x+4 s̅ y−1 (pair_dot, pair_bang), append, p1_bd, p1_bb, p1_db, p1_dd (two blocks merge), merge, end_db, next, end_b, restart2, and the rarer mid_db, merge_b, mid0_d, mid0_b; and the pair rule on the fuel block itself (own_dot, own_bang, with step counts).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 80,103 cells have been visited and 39,938 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The macro machine agrees with the machine
claims.text: py/check.py 2e7 checks every one of the sweeps of the first 2·107 steps against the macro rules. py/r14.c prints the tape at every refill (fuel 0) up to 1010 steps; py/cmp.py finds the macro machine equal to it at all 33 of them (74,633 sweeps).

claims.title: 187,450 sweeps inside the rules
claims.text: py/far.py runs the macro machine 187,450 sweeps (far past 1010 machine steps) and never meets a window or fuel case that its rules do not cover.

claims.title: 10<sup>2708</sup> sweeps of the block-list map
claims.text: py/blockmap.py (run-length lists, jumps across runs of equal blocks) runs 55,882 refills, 102708 sweeps, from blank tape. With six rules added (mid.!, merge!!, mid0., mid0! and two folds, each checked against the machine on random lists by py/check_rules.py), it never meets a window or fuel case outside its rules, and at every refill there is a done block to refill from. The jumps are checked against the plain map for the first 143 refills (py/check_jump.py).

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: No halt in the first 1.87×10<sup>14</sup> steps of an accelerated run
claims.text: Observed, not proved: the accelerated simulator rsim.py ran 1.87×1014 steps from blank tape without reaching a halting transition. Its tape, state and head position were equal to those of a plain C simulator at 6 checkpoints, the last at 1.21×1010 steps. Of these steps, the part after the last checkpoint rests on the simulator alone, including 1,392 trip-level jumps: a jump applies many identical round trips at once after seeing the same tape shape recur with constant count changes, which is validated against direct simulation but not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. A proof would need an invariant on the lists that the macro rules preserve (so that no window ever falls outside them), plus Lean proofs of the remaining cases: the sweep with fuel 1 (two rules in one visit), the windows with small values, and the rules on the fuel block other than the pair rule. The block-list map ran 10<sup>2708</sup> sweeps without a gap once six rarer rules were added, but rare new windows may keep appearing.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LE_1RC0LB_1RD1RF_1RE0RB_1LA0RD_0RE--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RF_1RC0RE_1LD0RB_1RE0LC_1RA0LE_0RC--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. The tape turns out to be a list of numbers, written as blocks of 10s, with a fuel counter at the left end. Each sweep of the head spends 2 units of fuel and does one small piece of arithmetic at the first unfinished block; when the fuel runs out, a finished block becomes the new fuel. Lean proves the sweep exactly; the rules have run 187,450 sweeps without a gap.

facts.text: Exact, for any list of done blocks and 12 window rules (Lean).
The macro machine equals the real run at all 33 refills.
The macro rules never meet a case they do not cover.
55,882 refills of the block-list map; the fuel never runs out and no window falls outside the rules (six rarer rules added).
No halt in the accelerated simulator (observed, not proved; checked against direct simulation up to 1.21×10<sup>10</sup> steps).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 80,103 cells (49,545 left of the start, 733 right), with a density of 1s of 0.499.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: The tape is a list of numbers
html: Watch the tape whenever the head, in state A, stands on the leftmost visited cell, on a 1. Read from there, the tape is blocks of 10 separated by single cells: a list v0 s1 v1 s2 v2 … of numbers (how many 10s) and separators (. for 0, ! for 1). The first number is a fuel counter N. Then come done blocks, each followed by the 5-cell separator 0 1 1 0 0 (. 0 ! 1 . in the list), and then the window, the first block that is not done:

sections.heading: One sweep: fuel −2, one rule at the window
html: From the left end the head runs right in state B. It crosses each done block, leaving it in a temporary form ((10)^w sep becomes (01)^(w−1) 1010101), does a few dozen steps of work at the window, and turns back in state A. On the way back it puts every block back, two cells further left, and at the left end the fuel has dropped by 2. The commonest rule is the pair rule: x s y → x+4 s̅ y−1 (the separator flips):

The sweep costs about 2 steps per cell of the done blocks plus 4 per 10 of the window. Lean proves it for every list of done blocks, by induction over the list (rpass, lpass, sweep_gen).

sections.heading: A dozen local rules
html: What happens at the window depends only on its first few entries (x is the value there):

windowbecomesLean

x ! 1 . / x ! 1 !x+4 . 0 . / x+4 . 0 !p1_bd, p1_bb
x . 1 !x+4 ! 0 !p1_db
x . 1 . zx+5+zp1_dd
x ! 0 ! z .x+4+z .merge
x . 0 . zx done, window 1 ! znext
x . 0 . 0 . 0 ! 1 .x done, window 2 ! 1 .restart2
x sep 1 ! 0 at the endx sep 2 sep 1 ! 0append
x ! 0 / x . 0 ! 0 at the endx+1 done, 1 ! 0 / x+4 ! 0end_b, end_db
x . 0 ! z, z ≥ 2x done, window 3 . z−2mid_db
x ! 0 ! z !x+4+z !merge_b
x . 0 ! 0 . w / x . 0 ! 0 ! wx+4 ! w / x+6 . w−2mid0_d, mid0_b (never used so far)
x . 0 ! 0 ! 1 . zread as the single value x+3+z; the sweep goes on to the next windowtested only
x ! 0 . z (not at the end)read as the single value x+1+z; the sweep goes ontested only
The last five rows are rarer windows that first appeared far out in the run (from sweep 2·1016 on); each was read off the real machine and checked on thousands of random lists (py/check_rules.py).

When the window is the fuel block itself, its own pair rule runs (own_dot, own_bang). When the fuel is 0, the sweep refills it: the list 0 sep v1 … becomes 2 . v1 …, so the first done block joins the fuel (sweep_gen0). Fuel 1 is a special case where one visit applies two rules; that case is not yet proved in Lean.

sections.heading: Carries and powers of four
html: Each refill turns the leftmost done block into fuel, and the fuel pays for pair rules that multiply the window by about 4 while counting its neighbour down. Many of the done blocks that result have the form 4k−2 (2, 14, 62, 254, 1022, 4094, 16382, …), and long runs of 2-blocks pile up at the right end. The list at the refills (computed by the macro machine; the step numbers are from the C run):

The run is like an odometer with irregular digits: the big blocks on the left grow by factors of 4, the short blocks on the right accumulate, and carries ripple through the middle. Every refill so far has been followed by enough work to reach the next refill; nobody has a proof that this always happens.

sections.heading: Running the fuel counter out
html: Does the fuel ever run out for good, with no done block left to refill it? py/blockmap.py runs the same macro machine on run-length lists, so a sweep costs a constant amount of work, and crosses a run of equal blocks in one jump once one block of it has shown the pattern. It equals py/mac14.py sweep by sweep (30,000 sweeps), and its jumps change nothing at the 143 refills a plain run reaches (2.2·1010 sweeps, py/check_jump.py).

In 50 minutes it ran 55,882 refills and 102708 sweeps. Every time the fuel reached 0 there was a done block to refill from, so the fuel never ran out. The exponent grows in a straight line, about 0.048 decimal digits per refill, so each refill multiplies the work by about 1.12. The list held 6,030 runs of equal blocks at the end, and the largest block had about 2,700 digits.

The first refills of the far run, written as before, show the powers of four taking over: 0 | 6 | 16777214×3 | 1685 | 4193877 | 4181686 | 262142×32 | 11338 ! 62701 | 65534×10 | … | 14×561076 | 10 | 2×2947758 | 1 ! 0 (refill 82). Blocks 4k−2 come in runs, a carry turns a run of 4k−2 into a run of 4k+1−2 as it passes, and the tail of 2-blocks grows to millions.

Six windows outside the old rules turned up along the way. The first, x . 0 ! z, at sweep 2.15·1016 (refill 226). Then a folding window at 10114, another at 10119, x ! 0 ! z ! at 10203, and nothing new after sweep 10873. None of them leads to the halting move. New rare cases may keep appearing, so this run is evidence, not a proof.

sections.heading: What is proved and what is missing
html: Lean, kernel: the cell pieces of a sweep (lean/Rules.lean, written by bbtools.symtm), one whole sweep for any done blocks and the window rules above, including three of the five rarer ones (lean/Macro.lean).
Computed: the full macro machine (py/mac14.py) checked against the machine sweep by sweep for 2·107 steps and at every refill up to 1010; 187,450 sweeps without leaving its rules.

Missing: the fuel-1 sweep, small-value windows, the two folding windows and the other fuel-block rules in Lean; a statement that puts all rules together as one map on lists; and an invariant showing the lists always stay inside the rules. Halting would need a window outside every rule; inside the rules proved in Lean the machine never reaches the halting move F1.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RF_1RC0RE_1LD0RB_1RE0LC_1RA0LE_0RC---: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→A, E→B, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state D, in a mirror

family: Counter with fuel (sweeps over a list of blocks; carries like base-4 arithmetic)
summary: The tape is a list of blocks of 10s; each sweep spends 2 units of a fuel counter on the left and applies one local rule at the first unfinished block. Lean proves one sweep exactly for any list of finished blocks and 12 window rules; the macro machine matches the real run to 10<sup>10</sup> steps and a run-length version of it runs 10<sup>2708</sup> sweeps (55,882 refills) without leaving its rules once six rarer rules are added.
